items.title: What can shoppers find at Food World Plus in Mississauga? International groceries, sushi, bakery goods and bulk items
items.summary: The store features international groceries, prepared foods and parking for 1,100 vehicles. Food World Plus has opened in Mississauga, with 176,000 square feet of retail space. A gigantic multicultural grocery store has opened in Mississauga with an extensive chocolate, candy and snack selection. But it’s not just the confections that are enticing shoppers to the new Food World Plus. Located at 50 Matheson Blvd. , the store has 176,000 square feet of retail space, featuring groceries from Europe, the Caribbean, the Middle East, East Asia and South Asia. A few of the items shoppers can find include: Plus, there’s a warehouse section similar to Costco for those who need to buy in bulk. “As a tourist, I have never had any desire ever to visit Mississauga. This changes all that,” @KirbyCub wrote in a TikTok post.

items.title: CVC updates 70-year-old plan to protect Credit River in Mississauga, Brampton
items.summary: Credit Valley Conservation is breathing fresh life into a decades-old document as it looks to better protect the Credit River Watershed from the northern reaches of the Greater Toronto Area to the mouth of the 90-kilometre-long river in Mississauga’s south end. The first Credit River Watershed plan was created in 1956, and CVC officials are currently nearing the end of a multi-year update to protect the diverse natural area for decades to come. “This new plan will use the latest science and data, as well as partner, stakeholder and community input to establish long-term priorities for CVC and municipal partners,” Credit Valley Conservation said in an update to the community. “It will set the stage for our scope of work for years to come,” CVC added. A watershed plan, conservation authority officials say, “is a tool that helps us understand the past and plan for the future health of the watershed. ” Credit Valley Conservation protects natural areas and watercourses in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon in addition to several other communities including Orangeville, other places in Dufferin County and Halton Hills.

items.title: Canada-wide award recognizes community facility in Mississauga
items.summary: A Mississauga hockey and multi-purpose arena has won a national award for operating with energy efficiency in mind. The City of Mississauga said Paul Coffey Arena, named for the Mississauga native and Hockey Hall of Fame member, has been chosen Energy Star Building of the Year by Natural Resources Canada. ” That work at Paul Coffey Arena, they added, earned the facility the national recognition this week. “We are proud to receive this award because it recognizes the practical work our teams are doing to make city buildings more efficient and more affordable to operate,” said Anna Cascioli, City of Mississauga director of facilities and property management. “At Paul Coffey Arena, upgrades to lighting, building controls and arena equipment, supported by better performance data, are helping us use less energy and manage costs. ” Formerly called Malton Arena, the facility serves that community with Learn to Skate, ice hockey, public skating, ball hockey and other recreation programs, the city said.

items.title: Mississauga Animal Services’ $25 dog, cat adoptions return on Monday
items.summary: Normal adoption fees are $280 for dogs and $190 for cats — it’s only $25 Nov. 2-14. Open to everyone, not just Mississauga residents. Messi the dog is one of many animals available for adoption at the Mississauga Animal Services shelter ahead of their November Adopt-a-thon. Dogs and cats will be available for adoption from Mississauga Animal Services in November for as little as $25. During the animal shelter’s Adopt-a-thon between Nov. 2 and 14, dogs and cats at the animal shelter will be available for adoption for $25, plus tax and any applicable pet licence fees. The event will be held at Mississauga Animal Services (735 Central Pky. m. , Monday through Saturday. That is well below the service’s normal adoption fees of $280 for dogs and $190 for cats, according to an Oct. 29 news release on Oct. 29. The event is open to anyone, not just Mississauga residents, the service said.

items.title: Walmart Canada launches AI shopping assistant Sparky
items.summary: MISSISSAUGA - Walmart Inc. has brought its AI chatbot Sparky to Canada, more than a year after the retailer first rolled out the shopping assistant in the United States. , on Wednesday, July 2, 2024. THE CANADIAN PRESS/Christopher Katsarov MISSISSAUGA - Walmart Inc. has brought its AI chatbot Sparky to Canada, more than a year after the retailer first rolled out the shopping assistant in the United States. The chatbot allows consumers to find and compare products or assist in building a shopping list. Andrew Go, vice-president of e-commerce at Walmart Canada, says Sparky can help consumers with questions and plan shopping lists based on a specific budget or an occasion such as a holiday meal. Walmart CEO John Furner last month vowed that its AI shopping assistant will not use personal information such as income or shopping history to set personalized prices for customers or hide lower-priced options. The pledge came as concerns grew from some shoppers skeptical about the rollout of digital price labels and the retailer’s push to integrate AI. Meanwhile, Loblaw Cos. Ltd. integrated its grocery delivery app into OpenAI’s chatbot ChatGPT in February — a first among grocers.

items.title: City Council's New Enforcement Rules Add $10 Charge When Parking Tickets Arrive by Mail
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga city council has approved a $10 fee that will apply whenever a parking infraction notice is delivered by mail instead of left on a vehicle's windshield. The outlet reports the charge took effect Oct. 1 alongside other changes to the city's parking enforcement rules, which now let bylaw officers record a licence plate and mail a notice to the registered owner when placing a ticket directly on the car would be unsafe or impractical. Insauga.com says enforcement officers will still affix tickets to windshields whenever it is safe to do so, and the mail option is meant as a fallback rather than a replacement. The outlet quotes Mississauga's community services commissioner, Raj Sheth, who told council that mailing a notice requires extra administrative work to prepare, process, print and send, which the new fee is meant to offset. According to insauga.com, the fee will be charged only in cases where a penalty notice is served by mail, not on tickets left on a windshield.

items.title: House of the week: Renovated bungalow with saltwater pool in Mississauga
items.summary: This place: A renovated bungalow in a sought-after Mississauga neighbourhood. Features: This renovated bungalow sits on a landscaped lot in coveted Lorne Park. The residence offers over 3,400 square feet of total interior space. The main level unfolds through an open-concept design with hardwood floors, pot lights and large windows in the living, dining and kitchen spaces. The kitchen anchors the home with direct views toward the backyard, a centre island and quartz countertops. The living room features a fireplace and a walkout. The primary bedroom offers a three-piece ensuite bathroom. Two additional bedrooms and a four-piece bathroom complete the main level. The basement features a recreation room, a second fireplace, two bedrooms, a three-piece bathroom, a laundry area and storage. An additional office/den provides a home workspace, games room, study or potential additional bedroom. A heated, saltwater, concrete pool is framed by landscaped grounds and patio space. The renovated cabana is complete with a television and an electronic roll-up door. A heated garage completes the package. Set within Lorne Park, the property offers access to schools, scenic walking trails, parks, recreational amenities, GO Transit, the QEW and Toronto Pearson Airport.

items.title: Fandoms unite for the Mississauga Comic Expo on November 6 and 7
items.summary: Assemble at Hazel McCallion Central Library for a two-day celebration of comics, gaming, art and fandom for all ages. Mississauga Comic Expo (MCX) is where fandom comes to life. Hosted by Mississauga Library, this free event invites everyone for a celebration of creativity, community and the stories that inspire us to connect, learn and discover. MCX features a lineup of workshops, panels, interactive activities and more. Suit up for the cosplay red carpet, strike a pose at the green-screen photo booth and browse the MCX Trading Post for unique finds. Learn the art of gag comics, build miniatures and draw in chibi-style. Try out new board games or test your skills in free-play video games and trivia contests. Stop by the Manga Lounge to connect with fellow fans and browse a wide selection of manga. Families can also enjoy fun activities including sketch challenges, Pokémon crafts, LEGO building activities and a dance party. Friday begins with fun activities and a superhero movie screening. m. m. m. , Mississauga.

items.title: Natural Resources Canada Honours Paul Coffey Arena for Energy Efficiency Gains
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, Paul Coffey Arena has received the ENERGY STAR Building of the Year Award from Natural Resources Canada after the city made a series of efficiency upgrades at the Malton facility. The city reports the arena serves the community with programs including Learn to Skate, ice hockey, public skating and ball hockey. According to the city, the retrofits cut energy use by about 5 per cent compared with a 2023 baseline and secured roughly $195,000 in incentives. The city says the project supports the Buildings and Clean Energy pathway in its Climate Change Action Plan, which targets a 40 per cent cut in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 and an 80 per cent cut by 2050, measured against 1990 levels. According to the city, Natural Resources Canada's ENERGY STAR Canada Awards recognize organizations and facilities that demonstrate leadership in energy efficiency, and officials say the arena's win reflects a broader citywide push to manage energy use and operating costs.

items.title: Mississauga Fire Crews Responded to 495 Carbon Monoxide Calls Last Year, More Than in 2024
items.summary: According to Mississauga Fire and Emergency Services, crews responded to 495 calls involving carbon monoxide in homes last year, up from 450 the year before. The department says it is marking Carbon Monoxide Awareness Week from Nov. 1 to 7 by urging residents to test their alarms and learn the warning signs. Mississauga Fire and Emergency Services reports CO is an odourless, colourless gas produced when fuels such as natural gas, propane, gasoline, oil and wood burn incompletely, with sources including fuel-burning appliances, fireplaces and vehicles left running in attached garages. According to the department, both people and pets can be harmed by the gas, and because it cannot be seen, smelled or tasted, dangerous levels can build up without warning. The department says exposure can cause serious illness or death, and that symptoms are often mistaken for other illnesses. Officials add that a working CO alarm provides the early warning needed to get outside and call for help.

items.title: Mayor-Elect Tedjo Pledges Aggressive Push for Long-Delayed Milton GO Expansion
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Mississauga mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo said expanding GO train service on the Milton line is among his top priorities as he prepares to take office next month. The outlet reports tens of thousands of Mississauga residents and workers, along with thousands more in Milton, have waited years for two-way, all-day service on the line, which serves stations in both municipalities en route to Toronto. Insauga.com says Ontario Premier Doug Ford backed the roughly $1-billion plan in early 2024 and called on the federal government to become a full funding partner. The outlet reports Ottawa committed in 2021 to cover half the project's cost, but a funding agreement has still not been finalized. According to insauga.com, Tedjo pledged at a Tuesday press conference, the morning after his decisive election win, to aggressively pursue the Milton GO expansion once he is sworn in Nov. 16.
